digest.component_or_area: Jira Data Center reconciliation harness and live verification suite
propositions: The epic's headline acceptance criterion requires proof that a DC-created issue appears in the local store after an inbound pass AND a local edit appears on the DC issue after an outbound pass, both against a realistic store copy with real ticket volume, not an empty store.

The copied store must be isolated from production: a fresh git repo with no remotes, REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off, no Cloud credentials, and scrubbed of all .bridge_state* artifacts and Jira bindings to prevent accidental writes to production.

The store copy verification must count LOCAL TICKETS directly (filesystem entries under .tickets-tracker/) to distinguish an empty local store from an empty remote instance, correcting the earlier misdiagnosis that scanned=0 proved the store was empty.

The inbound and outbound mutation suites must assert each of 28 mutations individually against named oracles (path assertions on rebar show / DC REST reads), not on aggregate convergence, with idempotence and pagination fully exercised.

Five product defects were discovered and fixed during this work: d067 (DC status never transitions), 8d68 (inbound update never mints identity), 751e (unassign never clears assignee), 2b16 (inbound link removal unsupported), 88d9 (inbound parent clear never emitted).

Live harness runs proved both directions of the headline AC green and surfaced structural issues (filter matching on inbound creates, disjoint emit/apply parent gates on DC, sub-task reparent silent no-op) requiring product fixes and test-oracle rewrites to avoid vacuous passes.
